description: The authors optimize water-network topology and pipe sizes for a real Belgian utility case involving De Watergroep. The comparison evaluates design choices under pressure, fire-flow and failure constraints. The reported optimized design reduces cost by 18.5 percent and has a 67 percent branched and 33 percent meshed composition. These are modelled design outcomes, not proof that the network was constructed or that future costs will match the estimate. The source establishes a documented infrastructure planning application; exact study dates, complete input data, solver availability and application to other municipalities remain unknown. Geographic coverage and temporal coverage are limited to explicitly named observations or benchmark applications; remaining coverage is unknown. Metadata and file descriptors were reviewed, with no dataset values, source code, model archives or paper bodies intentionally fetched. Public access to descriptive papers does not establish executable availability or rights to all linked components. Licence and cost for executable components remain as explicitly stated above or unknown. This supports infrastructure simulation and the specific source-defined modelling role.
